newsitem.title: UK: M & S, UK retailers down on low Xmas sales.
newsitem.headline: M & S, UK retailers down on low Xmas sales.

text.p: UK retailers Next Plc, Marks and Spencer Plc and Boots Plc saw their shares tumble on Friday, defying a firm FTSE 100, after the Daily Mail earlier reported low Christmas sales.
At 1630 GMT Marks and Spencer was down 2.4 percent or 11-1/2p at 472-1/2, Boots was down 9-1/2p or 1.6 percent at 596-1/2 and Next was down 7-1/2p or 1.2 percent at 544-1/2.
"It's been a very disappointing Christmas," said analyst Nick Bubb at Mees Pierson. "There will be a last minute rush, but it won't be enough to make up for it.
Bubb said the low sales had rocked retailers who expected strong December sales to follow what was a bright November.
The Daily Mail said figures from the British Retail Consortium suggested sales were static three weeks ago, down 0.6 percent two weeks ago, and down 1.6 percent a week ago.
But John Richards, analyst at NatWest Securities, said the nervousness was no real surprise to the markets.
"Nervousness ahead of Christmas is as traditional as pantomimes and mince pies," he said, "it happens every year." -- Catherine Bremer, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
